subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): expose anonymous Talk activity to plugins

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support a process-wide anonymous Talk activity observer for explicitly enabled plugins, with `contracts.talkActivityObservation: ["process-wide"]` as its public SDK entitlement?
rationale: The code is a new durable Plugin SDK and manifest contract, not a bug fix; maintainers must decide whether the lifecycle and timing metadata, its operator trust model, and its compatibility commitment belong in core.

options.title: Accept the explicit observer contract
options.body: Treat the manifest declaration plus explicit plugin enable as the approved boundary and support the documented redacted event stream as a stable Plugin SDK surface.

options.title: Defer the public API
options.body: Keep the capability out of core until maintainers choose a narrower or differently scoped plugin trust model for process-wide Talk metadata.

recommendation.title: Accept the explicit observer contract
recommendation.body: Treat the manifest declaration plus explicit plugin enable as the approved boundary and support the documented redacted event stream as a stable Plugin SDK surface.

likelyOwner.reason: RomneyDa authored the proposed observer and the adjacent merged shared Talk-session work, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the implementation details.
